In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gallbladder hypokinesia is the most important cause of gallstone formation in patients with gallbladder stasis.
gallstone formation is a multicausal disorder and that the gallbladder hypokinetic state is an important contributing factor.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gallstones are formed in a bile with a supersaturated cholesterol concentration, and that gallstones are retained in a gallbladders with a defective motor function.

the gallbladder is an organ with a high capacity to adapt to different conditions, and the gallbladder motor response to cholecystokinin (CCK) is an important determinant of the gallbladders capacity to handle bile.
the pathogenesis of gallstone formation involves the interplay between the liver, gallbladder and bile acids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gallbladder is a dynamic organ, and the motility defect is not an intrinsic abnormality but rather a consequence of the disease.

the gallbladder hypofunction may be the key to the development of cholesterol gallstones, and that the gallbladders of patients with cholesterol stones have a defect in their contractile response to CCK and to the calcium ionophore A-23187.
the gallbladder motor defect is a key factor for gallstone formation in humans and that it is possible to correct this motility defect by using different pharmacologic agents.
